key_insight: LLIFT creates semi-synthetic brain MRI lesions in user-controlled locations without needing pixel-level lesion labels, enabling ground-truth data for XAI evaluation.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers test whether explanation methods truly localize pathology in medical imaging more reliably than using manually labeled or artificially pasted lesions.
method: Trains a label-informed feature transfer framework from healthy and pathological brain MRI.
LLIFT-GAN learns pathological features from binary class labels only.
LLIFT-DM uses diffusion-based inpainting conditioned on bounding-box masks via ControlNet.
evidence_signal: On Human Connectome Project brain MRI data, both variants reached Fréchet Inception Distance scores comparable to the healthy-versus-pathological separation in the dataset, with qualitative inspection supporting lesion realism.
watch_item: The generated lesions are semi-synthetic, so realism and downstream XAI conclusions still depend on how well the benchmark matches true clinical pathology.
paper_title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches
